subject: Finex - Post-call: throughput & SLO qualification
messages:
From: Rafael Mendes <rafael.mendes@redwood.ai>
To: Alex Johnson <alex.j@finex.com>
Cc: Marissa Cole <marissa.cole@redwood.ai>
Date: Sat, 15 Aug 2026 09:05:00 -0700
Subject: Finex - Post-call: throughput & SLO qualification

Alex — great talking earlier. Quick recap from our discovery + a few follow-ups so we can size recommended capacity and confirm SLO alignment. Attaching a quick sizing snapshot (finex-throughput-snapshot.xlsx).

Call recap (high level):
- Primary workload: conversational assistant + document summarization for support use cases (chat-first, some streaming).
- Latency targets: p95 response (end-to-end) target ~250-300ms for single-turn text gen; streaming first-byte target <150ms where streaming is enabled.
- Typical response length: 350–550 tokens (avg ~450 tokens).
- Peak vs steady: you called out steady-state QPS ~20, peak bursts up to ~120 QPS (bursts lasting 5–15 minutes).
- Concurrency: active concurrent sessions ~100 at steady-state, higher during peak.

Follow-ups / asks for sizing accuracy:
1) Can you confirm the region you want us to prioritize? (we recommend us-west-2 for lowest latency to Finex infra).
2) For streaming: is it server->client chunked streaming (SSE/HTTP2) for incremental tokens, and do you expect many long-lived streams?
3) Any hard constraints on first-byte latency for the streaming path (we noted <150ms but want to confirm SLA needs)?
4) Do you have retention/encryption requirements beyond standard KMS (e.g., HSM)?

Initial sizing notes (see attachment for detailed calc):
- Avg tokens/sec (steady): QPS_steady * avg_tokens = 20 * 450 = 9,000 tokens/sec.
- Avg tokens/sec (peak burst): QPS_peak * avg_tokens = 120 * 450 = 54,000 tokens/sec (short windows).
- Concurrency impact: with ~100 concurrent sessions, KV cache hit patterns and batching will matter; recommend enabling prefix KV caching for repeated context to reduce compute.

Recommended next steps:
- You review the attached snapshot and confirm the region + streaming behavior.
- If that looks right, we’ll provision a short proof-of-load in a dedicated pool (can mirror production region) to validate p95 and first-byte streaming targets under your burst profile.

Attachment: finex-throughput-snapshot.xlsx (sizing assumptions + raw calc)

Best,
Rafael Mendes
Account Executive | Redwood Inference
rafael.mendes@redwood.ai
---
Redwood Inference — High-performance LLM inference

From: Alex Johnson <alex.j@finex.com>
To: Rafael Mendes <rafael.mendes@redwood.ai>
Cc: Marissa Cole <marissa.cole@redwood.ai>
Date: Sat, 15 Aug 2026 11:20:00 -0700
Subject: Re: Finex - Post-call: throughput & SLO qualification

Thanks for the clear recap, Rafael — this aligns with what we discussed. A few specifics to confirm on our side: 

- Region: us-west-2 is preferred.
- Streaming: yes, server->client incremental streaming (SSE) for chat. We have a mix of short (~50–150 tokens) and long (~400–800 tokens) responses depending on context; avg of ~450 is fine for sizing.
- First-byte latency: target is 120–150ms for streaming (we'd prefer <=150ms).
- Steady vs peak: steady QPS is about 20–25 during day-to-day, peak bursts (marketing incidents, ticket surges) can push up to ~120 QPS for up to 10 minutes.
- Concurrency: around 80–120 active sessions typically.
- Security: standard KMS is required; HSM is not required now but we may revisit for enterprise procurement.

One addition: for document summarization flows, we often fan-out 2–3 model calls per user action (summarize + rerank + final polish), so site-wide effective QPS for model calls could be 1.8x–2.5x the user-facing QPS depending on route. Worth accounting for in the sizing.

Looping in procurement (procurement@finex.com) for next steps on contract/licensing and any security forms.

—Alex
Alex Johnson
Staff Engineering Manager — AI Platform
Finex

From: Rafael Mendes <rafael.mendes@redwood.ai>
To: Alex Johnson <alex.j@finex.com>
Cc: Marissa Cole <marissa.cole@redwood.ai>
Date: Sat, 15 Aug 2026 13:45:00 -0700
Subject: Re: Finex - Post-call: throughput & SLO qualification

Alex — perfect, thanks for the details and for the fanned-call note (that’s important). I updated the sizing assumptions and attached a refined CSV (finex-refined-sizing.csv) with a steady vs peak breakdown and an “effective QPS” column that factors in the multi-call flows. Summary below.

Sizing summary (high level):
- Effective steady QPS: 20 user-QPS * 2.0 effective calls = 40 model-QPS.
- Effective peak QPS: 120 user-QPS * 2.0 = 240 model-QPS (short bursts).
- Avg tokens per model-call: 450 tokens -> steady tokens/sec = 40 * 450 = 18,000 tps; peak tokens/sec = 240 * 450 = 108,000 tps.
- Concurrency: with streaming and long responses concurrently, plan for ~120–200 concurrent model executions during peak.

Recommendation (starting point):
- Proof-of-load in us-west-2 using a dedicated pool sized to handle 40 model-QPS steady and validated against 240 model-QPS burst (we can autoscale to absorb bursts but need headroom for first-byte target).
- Runtime config: enable prefix KV caching for common prompts, moderate batching (target batch formation <= 20ms to preserve latency), and aggressive early-stream flushing for first-byte.

What we’ll validate in the proof-of-load:
- p95 end-to-end response <= 300ms for non-streamed flows, and first-byte streaming <= 150ms for streamed flows.
- Token throughput and queuing behavior during 10-minute bursts at 240 model-QPS.

I put the numeric calc in the CSV and included an example autoscale policy (burst to X nodes for up to 15 minutes). If this looks good I’ll:
1) schedule a 1-hour proof-of-load window next week (you pick a 1-hour slot)
2) open a deal in HubSpot and share a simple SOW for the proof-of-load + staging costs

Attachments: finex-refined-sizing.csv (detailed numbers + autoscale example)

Thanks — I’ll wait for the procurement contact and your preferred slot.

Best,
Rafael Mendes
Account Executive | Redwood Inference
rafael.mendes@redwood.ai
